content:
Maya: Quick question — how should the console + API surface model automatic degrade behavior for rollouts? I want something that's clear in the UI, auditable, and avoids surprising customers. Thinking of calling it 'graceful degrade' with discrete modes: model-substitute, cached-response, reject-with-retry, circuit-breaker.
Arjun: +1 to a named list of modes. Implementation-wise I prefer a route-level policy with account defaults. Triggers we should support: p95 latency > threshold for T seconds, 5xx spike %, OOMs/memory pressure, and explicit capacity shortage events from scheduler.
Leo: UX note: show the metric snapshot that fired the trigger next to the action taken. e.g. "p95 820ms > 500ms for 3m" — users need the 'why'. Also a small timeline that shows when it flipped and what fraction of traffic was affected.
Jess: API surface question — do we add separate endpoints like POST /routes/:id/degrade or expose a single /policies resource? I vote policies: one resource with structured actions and matchers.
Arjun: Example policy shape (draft):
```
{
  "policy_id": "pol-2025-09-grace-1",
  "scope": "route:/generate",
  "modes": ["model-substitute","cached-response"],
  "triggers": [
    {"type":"p95_latency","threshold_ms":500,"window_s":180},
    {"type":"error_rate","status_codes":"5xx","threshold_pct":1.0,"window_s":120}
  ],
  "canary": {"percent":10,"duration_s":600},
  "autorun": true
}
```
Leo: Nice. We should include a 'quality_guard' field too — evaluate a small eval set or monitoring signals and abort fallback if quality drop > X.
Maya: Agreed. Also need audit requirements: every automatic action must record: policy_id, trigger_snapshot (metrics + timestamp), decision (mode used + model/version), correlation_id, and whether user override exists. This should be queryable and exportable.
Jess: Billing/quotas: if mode=model-substitute we may change unit cost (e.g., quantized model cheaper). The console and billing pipeline must reflect actual variant used per token.
Arjun: Telemetry: tag traces/requests with policy_id and action_id. Emit a metric series for "policy_invoked" with labels (route, mode, trigger_type). Those will be critical for regression alerts and postmortem.
Maya: UX features I'd like: preview/simulate in console (run on sampled traffic), ability to set a grace-period (apply only after N triggers within M minutes), and a rollback window where the system auto-reverts if quality dips.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: policy pol-2025-09-grace-1 applied to route /generate at 2025-09-12T15:02:12Z, action=model-substitute->redwood/ggml-small-q4, trigger=p95>600ms
Jess: We should allow enterprises to mask model identifiers in the UI for compliance — add a redact flag to audit views.
Leo: Defaults proposal for self-serve: p95=500ms, 5xx>1%, sustained window=2m. Enterprise: keep editable. Retention: 30d for free tier, 180d for enterprise for audit logs.
Arjun: I'll draft an RFC for the /policies resource + telemetry conventions and paste a link here when done.
Maya: Great. Follow-ups: 1) default thresholds and sane presets, 2) audit log retention policy and export options, 3) console copy that explains "why this happened" to customers. We'll review in Thursday eng-platform sync. Filing a ticket to track: INT-1234.
Leo: :thumbsup:
Jess: Thanks — will add billing hooks to the ticket.
Maya: Thanks everyone. Small action items assigned in INT-1234.
